units.translation: The divine remains, even in a servile mind.
The revel remains in the house.
We will remain thus.

I would no longer remain, where in both places in M ἀμμείναιμ᾽ ἐγώ [I would remain] is written, which in the former place was corrected from Tzetzes in Cramer's Anecdota Oxoniensia vol. 3 p. 358, in the latter by Robortello.
For it remains.
Both, to remain and to send these.
And may these things remain forever.
I remain to hear how the contest will be decided.
But the oracles, no longer pure, he will prophesy while remaining, where νέμων [distributing] is more probable, which Hermann restored.
I remain to hear the outcome of this justice.
You might remain then; but if you do not wish to remain –
What honor remains for me?
The wrath of Zeus, protector of suppliants, remains.
So as to remain steadfastly.
In the same place, line 1002, a spurious and corrupt verse, about which I spoke under the word κάλωρα, reads μένην [to remain], with ει written above, i.e. μένειν [to remain].
The report of the Palici will rightly remain.
It is necessary to remain at home for the one who is truly fortunate; [and for the one who fares badly, he too must remain.]
Whoever, while remaining, rouses the cry of the trumpet, where Tyrwhitt restored κλύων [hearing], which the scholiast reads, who explains it as ἀκούων σάλπιγγος [hearing the trumpet].
But iron-bound fetters await them.
Instead of the ancestral altar, a block awaits.
The sorrows in the space between darkness remain for those who delay.
For fate awaits both the free man.
Fate has long remained.
The appointed end remains.
There is a place where the terrible thing must remain seated. Thus the anonymous writer in Dobree for δειμαίνει [he fears].
I cull a mournful fear, waiting for friends, if there is any protector of this flight from the Asian land. Thus Hermann for δειμαίνουσα [fearing].
It remains to pay with the spear a like penalty.
Why do you wait for those more powerful than these?
For the contest does not await men who are left behind.
Who, without trembling, will await a boasting man?
How then could they await enemy invaders?

something

and not, nor

nor, when the preceding clause is either affirmative or, much more frequently, negative. μηδέ [nor] and the other compounds with μή [not] differ from οὐδέ [nor] and the compounds with οὐ [not] in the same way as μή [not] and οὐ [not]: about which see above under μή.
μηδέ [not even] not even.
μηδέ [nor] nor, is constructed with the same moods and tenses as μή [not], as we showed above. Examples of this kind have been collected by Wellauer.
With the present subjunctive.
With the aorist subjunctive.
With the aorist imperative.
With the optative.
μηδείς [no one] no one. There are no examples of the masculine μηδείς [no one] and feminine μηδεμία [no one] in Aeschylus, but μηδέν [nothing] is frequent.
μηδέν [nothing] adverbially for simple μή [not].
μηδέπω [not yet] not yet.
Μηδικός [Median] Median or Persian.
μήδομαι [I devise] I think, I plan, I contrive.
μῆδος [counsel] counsel.
